t:
Section 401 of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3161) is amended as follows:

    (1) 
Paragraph (2) of subsection (a) is amended by striking out “40 per centum” and inserting in lieu thereof “50 per centum”.
 
    (2) 
Paragraph (6) of subsection (a) is amended to read as follows: 


“(6) 
those communities or neighborhoods (defined without regard to political or other subdivisions or boundaries) which the Secretary determines have one of the following conditions:

“(A) 
a large concentration of low-income persons;


“(B) 
rural areas having substantial outmigration;


“(C) 
substantial unemployment; or


“(D) 
an actual or threatened abrupt rise of unemployment due to the closing or curtailment of a major source of employment.
No redevelopment area established under this paragraph shall be subject to the requirements of subparagraphs (A) and (C) of paragraph (1) of subsection (a) of section 101 of this Act. No redevelopment area established under this paragraph shall be eligible to meet the requirements of section 403(a) (1) (B) of this Act; 


“(7) 
those areas where per capita employment has declined significantly during the next preceding ten-year period for which appropriate statistics are available.”

fable.w: The section amends the criteria for designating redevelopment areas, and the Secretary makes these determinations alone, with no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or advisory body involving anyone outside the federal government. The tempting reading is that mentioning communities and neighborhoods implies local involvement, but they are only the subjects of the federal determination, not participants in it.
fable.s: those communities or neighborhoods (defined without regard to political or other subdivisions or boundaries) which the Secretary determines have one of the following conditions

qwen_block.w: This section amends the criteria for designating redevelopment areas, specifying that the Secretary determines eligibility based on economic conditions like unemployment or low income. It does not require the Secretary to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or involve non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The determination is made solely by the federal official based on statistical or factual conditions.
qwen_block.s: those communities or neighborhoods (defined without regard to political or other subdivisions or boundaries) which the Secretary determines have one of the following conditions:

opus.w: This amendment only changes the criteria for designating redevelopment areas. The Secretary decides alone, and no outside party is consulted or given a hearing, comment period, advisory role or right to sue. The communities' role is to be eligible for designation, which is like eligibility for a benefit, not participation in the decision.
opus.s: those communities or neighborhoods (defined without regard to political or other subdivisions or boundaries) which the Secretary determines have one of the following conditions:
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** The amendment lets the Secretary decide which communities count as redevelopment areas. That could look like a procedural federal decision that affects localities.

**Why it fails:** The section only changes the eligibility criteria: a percentage threshold, conditions such as low income, outmigration and unemployment, and a declining-employment test. It does not require consulting states, local governments or the public. It does not set up a hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue, and it does not authorize rulemaking. The Secretary makes the determination alone, and communities qualifying for designation is an eligibility matter, not participation.

qwen_chat.w: The text only describes the criteria for the Secretary's determination and does not mandate any consultation or coordination with outside parties. It looks like participation because the Secretary makes a determination about communities, which might involve consulting with local officials.
qwen_chat.s: those communities or neighborhoods (defined without regard to political or other subdivisions or boundaries) which the Secretary determines have one of the following conditions:
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because the Secretary makes a determination about communities, which might involve consulting with local officials.
Resolution: The text only describes the criteria for the Secretary's determination and does not mandate any consultation or coordination with outside parties.
